newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds ended lower as the Swiss franc weakened and the market contemplated new supply via a federal government bond tender announced Tuesday.

The Swiss Treasury said this morning that it was reopening an outstanding bond maturing in June 2007. The reopened 4-1/2 percent bond was top of the list in terms of what traders had expected from this morning's offering. Traders quoted it 20 to 25 basis points below the outstanding paper.
Swiss markets generally focused on Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS)'s announcement of a restructuring which included news of a one-time 3.0 billion Swiss franc charge.

The UBS news was expected to have a long-term beneficial impact on the bank's earnings, but its shares fell sharply on the Swiss stock market, weighing on the entire market. The news was even cited as a factor weakening the franc.
UBS's outstanding bonds were liable to be unaffected despite news Standard & Poor's had put the bank on creditwatch.

"The difficulty in this market is that we don't have active bonds that trade. But had there been a recent UBS (bond) out there, I don't think it would have been affected, anyway. UBS is still one of the elite banks in terms of credit quality," said one bond trader at a Zurich-based foreign bank.

Some in the market was startled during during the morning by news the Swiss Treasury set a yield of only 1.25 percent on its latest three-month money market series SWIV of T-bills. The yield was far below 1.629 percent set on the previous week's issue of the Treasury bills. The issue garnered 1.141 billion Swiss francs for the government, versus 966.15 million at the previous tender.

"They (the Treasury) are getting a free lunch," said one trader of the government's latest pricing. A Treasury spokeswoman said the offer was filled at the low rate because a large amount of bids submitted were at "best price."
Dec Conf futures CONFZ6 down 19 at 114.76.
